justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are represented across elements like WebRTC Media Containers, Consent Management Container, and FHIR/E-Prescription Adapter Containers. However, the AI symptom checker is only generically mentioned inside the Core Business Logic Container without dedicated components for urgency scoring or triage workflows.
justifications.performance_efficiency: The design effectively addresses performance through Geo-DNS and Anycast IP Router, Regional Caches using Memorystore, and asynchronous messaging via Regional Pub/Sub Topics with Claim Check Handler offloading large payloads to GCP Cloud Storage.
justifications.compatibility: External interoperability requirements are thoroughly supported by dedicated components: US HL7 FHIR Adapter interfacing with US HL7 FHIR Providers, EU E-Prescription Gateway Adapter communicating via national protocols, and Pharmacy Network Coordinator managing Regional Pharmacy Networks.
justifications.usability: The Offline-First Patient Mobile/Web App specifically targets rural patients with low bandwidth. However, Licensed Clinicians lack a dedicated interface or portal container tailored to clinical consultation workflows, electronic prescribing, or reviewing symptom checker outputs.
justifications.reliability: WebRTC Media Containers provide degraded streaming under low bandwidth, while Offline-First Patient Mobile/Web App provides Local Database Storage, Transactional Outbox, and Network Resilience Manager. Regional Pub/Sub Topics incorporate dead-letter queues and circuit breakers across adapters.
justifications.security: Strict regional residency is enforced by Region Router and GCP Secret Manager. Privacy and accountability are guaranteed via Consent Management Container (OPA), Client-Side PII Redactor, Cryptographic Envelope Manager, and immutable trace storage in Traceability Logging Container.
justifications.maintainability: Hexagonal Architecture and Anti-Corruption Layers in Core Business Logic Container and FHIR/E-Prescription Adapter Containers decouple external protocols. Traceability Logging Container and OpenTelemetry Collector Sidecars provide observability, though Core Business Logic combines several disparate sub-domains into one container.
justifications.portability: The architecture satisfies multi-region GCP constraints (europe-west3 and us-central1) using containerized microservices. However, heavy coupling to proprietary cloud services (GCP Memorystore, Pub/Sub, and Secret Manager) limits portability outside of Google Cloud Platform.

PERF-01.justification: WebRTC Media Containers and stateless regional scaling handle concurrent video sessions. However, detailed media relay autoscaling (e.g., TURN/SFU fleet management) is not explicitly detailed.
elements: Core Business Logic & Video Consultation Containers
sensitivity_points: Dynamic scaling capacity of WebRTC media streaming containers under localized surges
Connection setup latency through Geo-DNS routing and authorization middleware
tradeoffs: Direct WebRTC streaming optimizes latency at the cost of complex regional scaling

PERF-02.justification: Peak load of ~14 requests/sec is modest; regional caching and decoupled core containers readily support it. Inference execution resource provisioning inside the core business container is less specified.
sensitivity_points: Latency overhead of synchronous AI inference execution inside business logic containers
Cache hit ratio for reusable symptom triage queries
tradeoffs: Synchronous symptom evaluation improves user responsiveness but risks compute contention

AVAIL-01.justification: Explicitly addresses degraded bandwidth via adaptive WebRTC streaming, network resilience managers, local database persistence (SQLite/IndexedDB), and transactional outbox queues preventing lost notes.
sensitivity_points: Client-side adaptive bitrate threshold handling below 300 kbit/s
Transactional outbox replay reliability after intermittent disconnection
tradeoffs: Client-side persistence and outbox queuing add app complexity to guarantee zero data loss

AVAIL-02.justification: The design enforces regional residency in us-central1, but lacks automated disaster recovery or a secondary US region to rebuild and restore US services within 1 hour during complete regional failure.
elements: Core Business Logic & Video Consultation Containers
sensitivity_points: Absence of secondary intra-US cold/warm standby region deployment
Regional data lock prevents failover to EU without violating residency constraints
tradeoffs: Strict regional residency prevents cross-region disaster failover, impacting availability during outages

MOD-01.justification: Containerized adapter architecture and anti-corruption layers isolate external prescription standards, confining changes strictly to the EU E-Prescription Gateway Adapter without touching core domain services.
sensitivity_points: Modularity of the EU gateway adapter interface abstraction
Decoupling of national protocol specifications via anti-corruption layers
tradeoffs: Dedicated adapter abstraction increases deployment surface but guarantees domain isolation

MOD-02.justification: Traceability Logging captures inputs and outputs to immutable storage, but runtime model versioning, parallel deployment, and rollback orchestration mechanisms are not articulated within the core container.
sensitivity_points: Audit trail schema consistency across updated model versions
Capability to dynamically switch or rollback model versions at runtime
tradeoffs: Asynchronous trace collection protects throughput but complicates real-time logging validation

SEC-01.justification: The architecture incorporates OPA policy evaluation, consent caching, authorization middleware at the region router, and audit logging sidecars to block unconsented cross-border data requests.
sensitivity_points: Strict enforcement of policy boundaries before dispatching cross-region gRPC requests
Completeness of immutable audit log generation for denied access attempts
tradeoffs: Centralized authorization checks introduce slight latency to ensure strict cross-border compliance

SEC-02.justification: Consent updates are distributed via GCP Pub/Sub push buses and invalidated in regional Memorystore caches, ensuring prompt policy propagation with audit logging verifying the change.
sensitivity_points: Message delivery latency and cache invalidation propagation across distributed regions
Downstream data-sharing consumers respecting newly revoked OPA policy tokens
tradeoffs: Cache-aside consent caching improves evaluation speed but introduces short cache invalidation windows
